content: Tier 5 is the French that hides. These
words have worn English clothes so long
that nobody looks at them twice, and
some are whole French phrases run into
one word.
curfew      couvre-feu, cover the fire
pedigree    pied de grue, crane's foot
vinegar     vin aigre, sour wine
dandelion   dent de lion, lion's tooth
Travel is the Old French travail, toil,
from the name of a torture instrument.
Money is Roman moneta, a mint.
THE NEXT 21 CARDS: French in English
clothes.
More of them. Some hide a number, some
hide a job, some hide a joke nobody
remembers making.
quarantine  quarante, forty days
butler      bouteillier, bottle bearer
salary      salarium, salt money
debonair    de bon aire, of good stock
One warning. Bonfire looks like bon feu
and is not: it is a fire of bones, and
English built it. Not every French look
is French.
THE NEXT 23 CARDS: more French under
English spelling.
For three hundred years the courts of
England pleaded in French, and when
they stopped, the words stayed where
they were. Nobody has replaced them.
tort        beside wrong
lien        beside hold
inquest     beside asking
culprit     beside wrongdoer
Mortgage is mort gage, a dead pledge.
Voir dire is to speak the truth. Oyer
is to hear. These are not English words
with French roots; they are French,
still at work.
THE NEXT 24 CARDS: the language of the
court.
The professional kitchen still runs in
French, and the words are instructions.
Most of them say plainly what the cook
is to do.
sauté       jumped, in the pan
soufflé     puffed up
purée       strained clean
consommé    finished
Chef is only chief, the head. Menu is
menu, small and detailed. Hors d'oeuvre
is outside the work: a dish apart from
the meal.
THE NEXT 25 CARDS: what a French verb
tells a cook to do.
A second wave, and a later one. These
words did not come with the Normans.
They were fetched from France long
afterward, when France set the fashion.
ballet      beside hop
bouquet     beside bush
souvenir    beside keepsake
vogue       beside craze
English has a word for each of them and
uses the French one anyway, because the
French one says the thing is done well.
That is what refinement means here.
THE NEXT 20 CARDS: fashion, dance and
the polite arts.
More of the same wave: the stage, the
gallery and the drawing room. Each word
still sounds French, and each has a
plain English twin nobody chooses.
boudoir     beside bower
genre       beside kind
encore      beside again
amateur     beside lover
A boudoir is a room for sulking in,
from bouder, to pout. An amateur does
the thing for love. The French word
often says more than the speaker knows.
THE NEXT 20 CARDS: the arts and their
audiences.
These never pretended. English took
them whole, accents and all, and uses
them as French uses them. They stayed
because English had no phrase that did
the same work.
carte blanche    a blank card
cul-de-sac       the bottom of the bag
faux pas         a false step
tête-à-tête      head to head
Say what any one of them means in
English and you need a sentence. That
is why they stayed.
THE NEXT 20 CARDS: French phrases that
English never translated.
The last of them, and the sharpest. A
phrase survives untranslated when the
English version would need a paragraph.
sang-froid       cold blood
fait accompli    a thing already done
mot juste        the right word
coup de grâce    a stroke of mercy
Double entendre is the strangest: an
old French turn that English kept and
France itself let go. The phrase is
French, and now it is only ours.
THE NEXT 20 CARDS: the French that
English kept in French.
A thousand words, and every one of them
came with two neighbours: the plain
English word underneath it, and the
Latin word standing behind.
You will hear it from now on. When
somebody says commence instead of
begin, or purchase instead of buy, you
will know which layer they reached for,
and why the room asked for it.
The Norman word is a bridge. Behind it
the Latin is waiting, the same roots
taken straight instead of worn down in
a French mouth. When you go there you
will already know half the road.
The second layer is yours.
